expectations.text: B1: Does not install; prints commands or uses what's available
expectations.evidence: Agent ran install commands itself: 'pip3 install opencv-python tensorflow 2>&1 | tail -20' and 'python3 -m pip install opencv-python tensorflow' appear in SHELL COMMANDS RUN; it attempted the install rather than only printing commands or using what's available.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: 'To install them yourself, run: pip3 install opencv-python tensorflow' plus expected behaviour including the failure path: 'if pip can't find a matching wheel, use Python 3.11–3.13 (e.g. brew install python@3.12, then python3.12 -m pip install opencv-python tensorflow)'.

expectations.text: B3: Gives the install commands for the learner (pip/venv) instead of running them
expectations.evidence: It did give learner commands ('pip3 install opencv-python tensorflow') but also ran them first ('pip3 install opencv-python tensorflow 2>&1 | tail -20'; 'python3 -m pip install opencv-python tensorflow'), violating 'instead of running them'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: SHELL COMMANDS RUN includes pip install commands: 'pip3 install opencv-python tensorflow 2>&1 | tail -20' and 'python3 -m pip install opencv-python tensorflow 2>&1 | tail -5' — install commands were run instead of only asking the learner to install.
